ui.cultureTipsHint: How things usually go at a Dutch workplace. Tap a tip to read it again.

gloss.c.je.b: At work most people say "je" to each other, often also to the boss. If you are not sure, start with "u" and listen to what others do. Saying "je" is not rude here.
gloss.c.je.s: Your new supervisor says: "Zeg maar je, hoor!" What does she mean?
gloss.c.je.o1: She wants you to say "je" to her.
gloss.c.je.w: "Zeg maar je" is friendly: she wants less distance. It is normal to say "je" to a supervisor in many Dutch workplaces.
gloss.c.names.b: On your first day, give a short handshake, look at the person and say your first name. Colleagues and managers usually use first names.
gloss.c.names.p: Hi, I am Ali. I am new here.
gloss.c.names.s: A colleague walks up to you: "Hoi, ik ben Mark." What do you do?
gloss.c.names.o1: Shake hands and say your first name.
gloss.c.names.w: A short introduction with your first name is the normal start. It helps colleagues remember you and ask you along.
gloss.c.arrive: Your first day: where to go
gloss.c.arrive.b: On your first day, go to the reception or the main entrance first. Say your name, your agency if you have one, and who you must see. Many companies give you a buddy: you may ask them everything.
gloss.c.arrive.p: Good morning, I am Ali. I start today. Who should I go to?
gloss.c.arrive.s: It is 6:45 on your first day. The gate is shut. There is an intercom. What do you do?
gloss.c.arrive.o1: Ring and say your name, your agency if you have one, and that you start today.
gloss.c.arrive.o2: Wait at the gate until someone comes out.
gloss.c.arrive.o3: Walk around the building to find another door.
gloss.c.arrive.w: The intercom is there for visitors and new workers. When you say who you are, they can call the right person.
gloss.c.ask.b: Asking a question shows you want to do the job well. Nodding when you do not understand can lead to mistakes or accidents. Asking again is completely normal.
gloss.c.ask.p: Sorry, I do not understand. Will you explain it once more?
gloss.c.ask.s: Your supervisor explains a task very fast. You did not understand it. What do you do?
gloss.c.ask.o1: Say that you did not understand and ask again.
gloss.c.ask.o3: Wait and hope someone else does it.
gloss.c.ask.w: Dutch supervisors expect questions. It is better to ask twice than to make a mistake.
gloss.c.gear.b: Rules about helmets, shoes and gloves are not a suggestion: everyone follows them, also the boss. Your employer must give you the protective gear you need, for free. Gear that does not fit does not protect you well, so ask for your size: "Heeft u dit in mijn maat?"
gloss.c.gear.p: My gloves are broken. Where do I get new ones?
gloss.c.gear.s: Your gloves are torn. What do you do?
gloss.c.gear.o1: Ask your supervisor for new gloves.
gloss.c.gear.o3: Quietly buy new gloves with your own money.
gloss.c.gear.w: Protective gear is the employer’s job. Asking for it is normal and shows you take safety seriously.
gloss.c.unsafe: Say it when it is unsafe
gloss.c.unsafe.b: If something is dangerous, say it right away, also to your boss. You may stop work that is really unsafe. Report accidents and near-accidents, even small ones.
gloss.c.unsafe.s: A pallet is stacked too high and almost falls. Nobody was hurt. What do you do?
gloss.c.unsafe.o1: Warn colleagues and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.unsafe.o3: Fix it alone and tell nobody.
gloss.c.unsafe.w: A near-accident is a warning. Reporting it helps prevent a real accident. Your employer may not punish you for reporting it.
gloss.c.accident.b: Tell your supervisor or the BHV’er (the company first-aider) about every accident, also a small one. Working through an agency? Tell the agency too. In an emergency, call 112 first. The company where the accident happened must report a serious accident to the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie (also if you work through an agency): when someone dies, is hurt for life or must stay in hospital. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.accident.p: My colleague is hurt. Where is the first-aider?
gloss.c.accident.s: You hurt your back while lifting. You are afraid to lose your job. What do you do?
gloss.c.accident.o1: Tell your supervisor today, and your agency too if you work through one.
gloss.c.accident.o2: Say nothing, so you do not lose your job.
gloss.c.accident.o3: Wait and see if the pain goes away by itself.
gloss.c.accident.w: Report it the same day, also if it seems small: the pain can get worse later. Your employer is not allowed to punish you for reporting it.
gloss.c.notyet.b: Your employer must explain how to do your work safely. Do not use a machine or forklift that nobody taught you. Saying "nog niet geleerd" is normal here: it shows that you work safely.
gloss.c.notyet.p: I have not learned this yet. Can you show me how?
gloss.c.notyet.s: A busy morning. Your supervisor says: "Pak jij even de heftruck? Het is makkelijk." You have never driven a forklift. What do you do?
gloss.c.notyet.o1: Say that you have not learned it yet. Ask for instruction, or for other work.
gloss.c.notyet.o3: Say "ja" and hope that it goes well.
gloss.c.notyet.w: A forklift without instruction is dangerous, for you and for others. Asking for instruction or other work is normal, also when it is busy.
gloss.c.direct.b: Dutch colleagues often say things very directly, like "Dat is fout" or "Doe het zo". They usually do not mean it rudely. You may also be direct, as long as you stay friendly.
gloss.c.direct.p: Okay, how should it be done then?
gloss.c.direct.s: A colleague says: "Nee, dat is fout. Die doos moet daar." What do you do?
gloss.c.direct.o1: Ask how it should be done and move the box.
gloss.c.direct.o3: Say nothing and leave the box where it is.
gloss.c.direct.w: Direct feedback is about the work, not about you. Asking "hoe moet het dan?" shows you want to learn.
gloss.c.limits: Say when it is too heavy
gloss.c.limits.b: Nobody expects you to lift everything alone. Saying "dit is te zwaar" and asking for help or a tool is smart, not weak. It protects your back.
gloss.c.limits.p: This box is too heavy. Can you help for a moment?
gloss.c.limits.s: You must lift a box that is much too heavy for you. What do you do?
gloss.c.limits.o1: Ask a colleague to help or use a cart.
gloss.c.limits.o2: Lift it anyway, so nobody thinks you are weak.
gloss.c.limits.o3: Leave it there and say nothing.
gloss.c.limits.w: Asking for help is normal teamwork. An injured back costs much more than a minute of help.
gloss.c.time: On time means a bit early
gloss.c.time.b: Being on time is very important. Many people arrive five or ten minutes before the shift starts. If you will be late, send a message or call before your shift starts, not afterwards.
gloss.c.time.p: Sorry, the bus is late. I will be there at eight.
gloss.c.time.s: Your bus is late and you will be 15 minutes late. What do you do?
gloss.c.time.o1: Message or call your supervisor right away.
gloss.c.time.o3: Do not go to work at all today.
gloss.c.time.w: Telling it early lets the team plan. Being late without a message is seen as much worse than the delay itself.
gloss.c.sick.b: Call your supervisor yourself, before your shift starts, unless your company has another rule. Working through an agency? Tell the agency too. You do not have to say what illness you have. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.sick.p: I am sick. I cannot come to work today.
gloss.c.sick.s: You wake up with a fever. Your shift starts at 7:00. What do you do?
gloss.c.sick.o1: Call your supervisor before 7:00 and say you are sick.
gloss.c.sick.o2: Ask a colleague to tell the boss later.
gloss.c.sick.w: Calling in sick yourself and on time is the rule in most Dutch workplaces. Your employer may ask how long it will take, but not what illness it is.
gloss.c.speakup.b: Here it is normal and respected to say calmly when something bothers you. Talk to the person first, at a quiet moment. Use "ik" sentences: "Ik vind het niet fijn dat ...". If it does not help, talk to your supervisor.
gloss.c.speakup.p: Something is bothering me. Can we talk for a moment?
gloss.c.speakup.s: A colleague always leaves the heavy work for you. It bothers you. What do you do?
gloss.c.speakup.o1: Calmly tell the colleague what bothers you.
gloss.c.speakup.o2: Keep quiet and get more and more angry.
gloss.c.speakup.o3: Complain about him to all other colleagues.
gloss.c.speakup.w: Dutch colleagues usually prefer to hear it directly. Saying it early and calmly keeps the relationship good.
gloss.c.no.b: When you say "ja", people count on it: an agreement is an agreement. So it is fine to say "nee" or "dat lukt niet" when you cannot do something. Say it in time and, if you can, offer another option.
gloss.c.no.p: No, that does not work today. Tomorrow I can.
gloss.c.no.s: Your supervisor asks if you can work extra on Saturday. You cannot. What do you do?
gloss.c.no.o1: Say no politely and offer another day.
gloss.c.no.o2: Say yes and then do not come.
gloss.c.no.w: A clear "nee" is respected. Saying "ja" and not coming breaks trust much more.
gloss.c.task: Say when it is done, ask when it is not clear
gloss.c.task.b: In the Netherlands a supervisor often gives a task in a few words, and expects you to say when it is done. Saying "ja" when you did not understand often leads to mistakes. Asking again, or asking to be shown, is normal here and not rude.
gloss.c.task.p: Done! What must I do now?
gloss.c.task.s: Your supervisor explains a task very fast. You understood only half. What do you do?
gloss.c.task.o1: Ask: "Kunt u het nog een keer laten zien?"
gloss.c.task.o3: Wait until a colleague does it.
gloss.c.task.w: Asking again is normal and takes a minute. Fixing a mistake takes much longer. Most supervisors would rather show it twice.
gloss.s.speakup.2: Can we talk for a moment?
gloss.s.speakup.3: I do not think that is fair.
gloss.s.agree.1: No, that does not work today.
gloss.s.agree.2: I do not agree with you.
gloss.d.agree.q: Can you work overtime on Saturday?
gloss.d.agree.a: No, that does not work. Sunday I can.
gloss.s.task.2: I am done with this task.
gloss.s.task.3: Can you show it one more time?
